text:
santiago: Quick heads-up — we're about to run the final observability preflight for eu-west-4 GPU pool tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Need a quick triage on logs/metrics/traces + cost guardrails before handing to infra ops.

maya: +1. Can you paste the checklist? I want to validate the alert templates and retention numbers.

santiago: Pasting the condensed checklist below — this is the runbook we want to follow during bring-up. Looking for any last-minute gotchas (network endpoints, S3 egress, NAT scaling).

santiago: RUNBOOK (condensed):
1) Networking: ensure VPC endpoints for S3 and Artifact Registry exist; verify NAT gateway autoscaling for control-plane egress.
2) Logging: deploy Vector sidecar + Loki stack, confirm promtail/Vector is shipping to central Loki cluster and local short-term store.
3) Metrics: Prometheus remote_write to central TSDB (long retention off-cluster); local Prometheus for node/memory metrics with lower retention.
4) Traces: Tempo deployed with s3 backend; verify sampling rules for GPU nodes.
5) Dashboards: Import base GPU-health + infra-cost dashboards into Grafana, set datasource to staging-eu-west4.
6) Alerts: Import alert templates, run `promtool check rules`, verify alertmanager routing for EU region.
7) Cost controls: set logging retention to 7d default, enable 10% tail-sampling for application traces.
8) Smoke tests + handoff: smoke logs/metrics/traces and push handoff message to #eng-oncall.

leo: Couple points:
- Make sure the S3 endpoint is in the region — we had one cross-region redirect last time that added 20% latency.
- NAT gw scaling: we should have a pre-warmed spare NAT or use PrivateLink for control-plane artifacts to avoid bursts.

tia: For alerts, I'm going to remove noisy GPU pod OOM alerts — they fire a lot during initial provisioning. I'll add a 15m suppression window for the node-level OOM alert.

santiago: Good call. Also: propose these concrete retention/cost knobs: logging retention 7d (default), index limit on Loki 250M/day, prom remote_write 30d, traces 14d with 10% sampling on app spans. Open to feedback.

maya: Sounds reasonable. For Loki: set chunk_target_size to 1MB and enable ingestion rate limiter at 50MB/s for the tenant to avoid cost spikes.

leo: Commands I'll run during smoke:
```
# check prometheus
kubectl get pods -n observability -l app=prometheus
kubectl exec -n observability prometheus-0 -- promtool check rules /etc/prometheus/rules
# check loki ingestion
curl -sS http://loki-observe:3100/ready
# check tempo
kubectl logs -n observability -l app=tempo | tail -n 200
```

santiago: Nice. I've also prepared a short validation script to run post-deploy (will run after manifests are applied):
```
#!/bin/bash
set -e
# 1) prometheus write check
curl -sS "http://prometheus.euw4.internal/api/v1/targets" | jq '.data.activeTargets | length'
# 2) grafana dashboards
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GRAF_TOKEN" "https://grafana.euw4.redwood/api/search?query=gpu-health" | jq 'length'
# 3) loki health
curl -sS http://loki.euw4.internal/ready
```

tia: Can you put that script in the runbook repo? I'll wire it into the Jenkins job so it runs automatically after deploy.

santiago: Yep pushing to repo now.

ops-bot: deploy-bot started: observability/eu-west-4-manifests @santiago (09:00 UTC)

deploy-bot: deploy status: manifests applied to cluster eu-west-4 — 6 resources created, 2 updated.

maya: After deploy, sanity checks I'll do: verify Prometheus targets, check `node_exporter` metrics for GPU nodes, confirm GPU driver exporter is on nodes, and validate alertmanager routes by sending a dry-run alert.

leo: For dry-run alerts:
```
curl -XPOST -d '{"labels":{"alertname":"TestAlert","severity":"critical"},"annotations":{"summary":"test"}}' http://alertmanager.euw4.internal/api/v2/alerts
```

tia: On cost side: I'll run a quick query against billing for logs ingestion from our dev projects to estimate daily MB/day and adjust retention if we spike.

santiago: One more networking check — confirm our private GKE control-plane IPs are allowed through corporate firewall rules and that the egress rule to S3 endpoint has the correct prefix list. Last time a missing prefix caused image pulls to fallback to public and slowed boot.

maya: I'll validate firewall rules and send a thumbs-up if all good.

leo: If anything breaks during bootstrap, fallback plan: 1) scale down GPU nodepool to 0, 2) toggle prom remote_write to false (stop long-retention writes), 3) escalate to oncall. Keep that in the runbook.

santiago: Copy that. I've updated the runbook with fallback steps and added a short checklist for the handoff message we post to #eng-oncall.

santiago: Handoff template (we'll post this after smoke):
```
Cluster: eu-west-4 (gpu)
Time: 2026-03-19 09:20 UTC
Status: smoke passed / failed
Checks: prometheus targets / loki ingestion / tempo ready / grafana dashboards
Known issues: <if any>
Fallback: scale nodepool->0, disable remote_write
Contact: @maya @leo @tia
```

tia: LGTM. Put me in contact line. :thumbsup:

maya: I'm happy to own the alerts/alertmanager routing validation during the handoff.

leo: I'll own the networking preflight (S3 endpoints / NAT).

santiago: Great — thanks all. I'll run the preflight at 09:00 UTC and post the handoff message once smoke passes. If someone can be around for 09:10–09:30 to triage.

deploy-bot: notify: scheduled deploy windows are configured, watchers: @maya @leo @tia

ops-bot: note: remember to set quota alarms for loki ingestion before enabling full traffic.

maya: Will set the quota alarms (Loki tenant -> 50MB/s, Prom remote_write -> 200k samples/s).

santiago: Perfect. Thanks team — will ping once started.
